entries.reason: iOS 10 computes it from three values iOS 6 already has, and the port computes the same expression
entries.effect: the timestamp plus the duration of a display frame times the frame interval, which is zero before the link has fired, as it is on the newer release
entries.source: the arm64 shared cache of iOS 12.0, disassembled, where the accessor ends in one fmadd of timestamp, duration and frameInterval; the armv7 caches of iOS 6.0 to 9.0, which have no such method, and the armv7s cache of 10.3.4, which has it

entries.reason: iOS 10 keeps the rate beside the frame interval and works the interval out from it; iOS 6 has only the interval, so the port keeps the rate beside the link and sets the release's interval by the same arithmetic
entries.effect: starts at zero, the documented default; setting a rate sets the release's frame interval to max(1, round(1 / (frame duration * rate))) and reads the rate back; where the application moves the frame interval itself, the rate reads back as the newer release converts it, 60 divided by the interval and truncated
entries.source: the arm64 shared cache of iOS 12.0, disassembled, for both setters, the shared helper and the literals 60.0 and 1/60; the header of iOS 16.4 for the default of zero
